claim: The Content section draws 33 boards and carries FOUR outbound cross-section edges in the whole prototype: back-to-editor, and three into Reference (two of them into [not-implemented] Commerce · setup).
truth: The founder's own example chain — Collections -> Fields -> Content -> Dynamic Page -> Data Binding -> Components -> Preview -> SEO -> Publish — is not navigable in the file AT ALL: zero Content->Pages, zero Content->Publish, zero Content->Preview, zero Content->Inspector edges. The code agrees it is not there: nothing in packages/editor calls cms.dynamicPages, and the Pages panel has zero CMS references (MOD-A-09).
evidence: Measured every prototype edge on page 1:3 this session with scripts/figma/module-graph.mjs: '06 · Content · 33  IN=109  OUT=4  reaches Journeys(1) Reference(3)'. Per-edge listing confirms the four are 148:2->52:2 (back), 148:2->304:2048, 151:46->303:2067, 775:4241->304:2048.
edit: Do not invent edges the product cannot walk. The honest fix is the opposite: the chain is broken in code, so the FILE must say so — a Module Interaction Map board that draws the chain with the broken links marked, plus [not-implemented] markers on any Content board that implies the chain works. Any wire-edge here waits on FIG-A's verdict on which hops exist.

claim: The edge map shows Client sign-off with 3 inbound and ZERO outbound cross-section edges — a section you enter and never leave. I briefed FIG-N that this was the most concrete defect in its family.
truth: That was wrong, and the boards say why in their own names. All 10 end '— echo of 1:6 (canonical); kept because Figma rejects cross-page NAVIGATE and the editor prototype must reach this state', and 1339:7193 says 'TERMINAL by design — the branch renders text + Signed as, zero controls (review-client.tsx:287-298,247-272)'. Client sign-off is a separate share-link surface, not an editor panel. Zero outbound is correct.
evidence: scripts/figma/module-graph.mjs TERMINAL list; then the section manifest read directly — every one of the 10 board names carries the echo clause. Correction sent to FIG-N before it could act on the wrong steer.
edit: No edge work. What IS unchecked: whether each echo still matches its counterpart on page 1:6, and the inline 'UNBUILDABLE' marker on 1339:7221 wants normalising to the file's [unreachable] convention.

claim: The Archive section fires 83 outbound edges into live sections, which reads at first glance as superseded boards still wired into the live prototype.
truth: Harmless in that direction, and the map proves it: Archive has ZERO inbound cross-module edges. Nothing live navigates INTO the archive. The 83 outbound are relics of each archived board's own rail and nav instances — 640:4202 alone accounts for ~30 through its Settings nav rows and rail. A reviewer who opens an archived board can leave it; nobody arrives there by accident.
evidence: module-graph.mjs: 'UNREACHABLE (no inbound cross-module edge): 27 · Archive · superseded · 20'; per-edge listing of 957:4474 shows every source is a [superseded ...] board and every hotspot is a rail/nav instance.
edit: None. Recorded so the next pass does not re-open it as a Critical.

claim: Section titles carry their own board counts ('05 · Media · 60'), which is exactly the kind of hand-maintained number that drifts.
truth: All 29 agree with reality. Claimed and real board counts match for every section, including the two the first census pass mis-read as empty (1779:2 Notifications 12, 1779:3 Command palette 13 — that was my pagination truncating at the MCP's 20000-character response cap, not the file).
evidence: Full census of 1:3: 29 sections, 905 boards, counted per section and diffed against the trailing number in each section name. Zero drift.

target: page 1:3 — 55 boards carrying a status marker
claim: The file marks boards the code cannot produce in FOUR different spellings: '[design-ahead] X' (23), '[not-implemented] X' (9), 'X — UNBUILDABLE — reason' (7), 'X — RETIRED <date> (reason)' (16).
truth: Three distinct claims are hiding in four spellings. 'The code has no producer but it could be built' and 'the product cannot produce this state by construction' are genuinely different, and both differ from 'superseded by another board'. The current set mixes them: 'Layers · empty — UNBUILDABLE — buildLayersFromEngine always emits a root row' is truly unreachable, while 'Layers · list-view — UNBUILDABLE — no list-view exists' is simply not built.
evidence: Census of all 905 board names on 1:3, grouped by marker: RETIRED 16, design-ahead 23, not-implemented 9, UNBUILDABLE 7.
edit: Normalise to three prefixes, PRESERVING each board's existing evidence clause verbatim (several already carry file:line, which is better than any replacement I would write): [not-implemented] no producer, could be built · [unreachable] cannot happen by construction · RETIRED superseded by another board. Apply with scripts/figma/apply-truth-marks.mjs, which reads every rename back from the file before reporting. Hold until the module lanes report so a rename does not race a proposal on the same board.

claim: FIG-I-01 filed a blocker: two competing 'Tree row' masters, and four Layers findings waiting on which one wins. Its recommendation was to keep 2142:11082 — the shared-chrome set with a Depth 0-5 axis and 387 instances — and port 243:6's five parts into it.
truth: There is no competition to adjudicate, and the recommendation rests on a false premise. Measured across page 1:3: 2142:11082 has 387 instances in Journeys (225), Shell (117), Templates (27), Reference (9) and Components (9) — and ZERO in Layers. 243:6 has 57 instances and every one of them is a Layers board. They are two different components that happen to share one name: a generic indented list row with a depth ladder and a label, and the actual Layers row with chevron, icon, name, eye and lock. Porting one into the other would have pushed five parts into 387 instances that never asked for them.
evidence: Walked every INSTANCE on 1:3 resolving getMainComponentAsync to its COMPONENT_SET; counts above. 2142:11082 is a COMPONENT_SET of 12 variants (Depth 0-5 × State rest/selected) whose first variant contains a single TEXT 'body'. 243:6 is a COMPONENT with 7 children starting 'tint-bg'.
edit: Both renamed so the collision cannot recur, and the Library section corrected — its name called 2142:11082 'the set every editor board instances', which is true of a list row and false of the Layers row. The four Layers findings are unblocked and target 243:6. What 243:6 genuinely lacks is a depth axis, while the product indents at 12 + depth×16 (LayerTreeItem.tsx) — that, not a merge, is the real gap.

claim: The closing verification pass — a render check of every changed board, a type/colour conformance sweep, and the 110 boards the lanes never opened — was dispatched and had to stop partway.
truth: The account's Figma MCP quota is a RATE WINDOW, not a hard cap. It reported "You've reached the Figma MCP tool call limit for your Full seat on the Professional plan" and every call failed — then a single probe minutes later returned normally. I filed it as a hard cap first and that was wrong in the direction that mattered: it would have written off three verification passes as impossible when they were merely expensive.
evidence: Exhausted by a seven-node inspection loop — one call per node, the worst possible shape. Recovered on a single probe with no intervention. The three verification agents were told to stop, then corrected and told to resume with pacing rules: aggregate inside the sandbox and return counts rather than node lists, batch several boards per call, never one call per node.
edit: No Figma action. The lesson is a method one and belongs with the tooling: a read shape that costs one call per node cannot survey a 927-board file, and every sweep in scripts/figma/ that does the walk INSIDE one use_figma call is why the rest of this arc fitted in the budget. A null result from an exhausted window is indistinguishable from a null result on a clean board, which is the confusion this arc has been fighting all day — so the probe, not the retry, is the right response to a limit error.

claim: The OVERPRINT detector found 8 text pairs whose boxes intersect, and a fixer narrowed the 'title' of each to the gap before its 'meta'.
truth: The heuristic — leftmost node is the title, rightmost is the meta — is right for a real title/meta ROW and wrong for two nodes that start at nearly the same x. There the gap is negative, the width clamped to a 40px floor, and a 248x48 paragraph became 40x256. It did that to three nodes, RECREATING the SQUEEZED class the same sweep had just cleared. Four of the seven were genuine rows and are correctly fixed; three were not rows at all.
evidence: Read back after the run: 164:65 40x256, 303:2072 and 303:2088 both 40x120, and the next sweep reported them as SQUEEZED and TEXTOVER. Geometry afterwards showed the real shape — 164:65 'This colour comes from your brand tokens' at (16,32) 248x48 with 'Open Brand' at (16,76): the paragraph wrapped to two lines and collided with the button row BELOW it. Vertical, not horizontal.
edit: All three restored to their original widths, then fixed vertically: the lower elements pushed past the paragraph's real bottom and the parent frame grown. The fixer now REFUSES rather than guesses — a repair that would take a node below 60% of its width or below 80px is reported for human eyes instead of applied.

claim: Five geometric detectors were in place — OUT, TEXTOVER, SQUEEZED, OVERPRINT, ESCAPES — and the sweep reported the file clean on four of them.
truth: A whole class was still invisible, and it is the one that does the most damage: a node INSERTED into a fixed-height panel whose spacer below was never shrunk. Everything downstream then overprints its neighbour or falls off the bottom. `Media · no-results` lost its ENTIRE footer — the Upload / Browse stock row sits at y827 inside an 812-tall board — and nothing reported it, because no child is out of ITS parent and no two text nodes intersect.
evidence: Found by eye by the lot-B visual pass, which also identified the mechanisable assertion: for a fixed-height panel, the last child's bottom must equal the panel height. On 145:250 the OVERPRINT the sweep did report was only a SYMPTOM — the cause was a spacer 28px too tall.
fix: check-panel-stacks.mjs asserts it across every 812-tall panel, skipping parked hotspots. This class silently DELETES a UI region from a spec: a reviewer sees a panel with no footer and cannot tell whether the product has one.

target: the Card / media component — 50 instances across 13 boards
claim: The clipped STOCK pill was filed as four defects on four Media boards.
truth: It is ONE component bug seen four times. The Card / media component has 50 instances across 13 boards, and every one that shows the hero-dark card carries the clipped pill. A single component fix retires all of them.
fix: Auto-width the pill with 6px horizontal padding, or widen the fixed pill to 48px — once, in the component. And the methodological half, which is worth more: a targeted clip-risk query over 116 boards returned 9 candidates and ALL were benign. Clipping does not correlate with tight geometry, because a clipped label's own measured width IS the clipped width — the node reports as fitting. No geometric test can see this class, so it is the one place where eyes are the only instrument.
